edits.text: 2. CONFIDENTIALITY. “Confidential Information” means non-public information disclosed by either party (the “Disclosing Party”) to the other (the “Receiving Party”) in connection with the Purpose, whether disclosed before or after signing and whether in written, oral, electronic, or other form, that is identified as confidential or reasonably should be understood to be confidential. The Receiving Party shall use Confidential Information solely for the Purpose and protect it with reasonable care, but no less than the care it uses for its own similar information. It may disclose Confidential Information only to its representatives who need to know it for the Purpose and are bound by confidentiality obligations at least as protective as those in this Agreement; the Receiving Party is responsible for their compliance. Confidential Information does not include information the Receiving Party can demonstrate was publicly available without breach, was lawfully known to it without a duty of confidence, was lawfully received from a third party without such a duty, or was independently developed without use of Confidential Information. If disclosure is legally compelled, the Receiving Party may disclose only what is required and, to the extent legally permitted, shall give prompt notice and reasonable cooperation in seeking protective treatment. On request, the Receiving Party shall promptly return or destroy Confidential Information, except for copies retained as required by law or routine backup procedures; retained copies remain subject to this Agreement. These obligations continue for five years from each disclosure, except that trade secrets remain protected for as long as they qualify as trade secrets under applicable law.
